item.title: Comment on *Atlantic Cataclysm* by mento
item.description:
I think the Arab Muslim slave trade which went on for 1300 years without interruption is more underrated. It was more brutal and killed more Africans than the Atlantic slave trade , 50% died during transport and male slaves were castrated.

It remains underreported, the only account I know of it is “ The Veiled Genocide” a book by Tidiane N'Diaye, a Franco-Senegalese author and anthropologist.

item.title: Comment on The Afrikaner exception by Naveen_K
item.description:
This isn't economic migration. If it was, I'd understand and would support the objection. But the issue is violence and persecution. Providing refugee pathways for Afrikaners while not extending the same to Black South Africans is logical under the circumstances. For decades, everyone was tip-toeing around the violence against White South Africans instead of speaking the plain truth because of political correctness concerns and SA's Apartheid past.

The fact that Black South Africans suffer more from poor governance isn’t directly relevant to granting refugee status to Afrikaners, given that White, particularly Afrikaner, South Africans are the primary victims of organized interracial violence. The murder rate for White farmers is so much higher than the already high murder rate in South Africa. While official South Africa crime statistics don’t explicitly break down murder rates by race, I’ve read that the interracial Black-on-White murder rate is as high as 95%. (Interracial crime in the US are also similarly one-sided, but no one except frog accounts on Twitter wants to talk about that).

South Africa has 47,000 White farming households, and over 3,000 farmers have been murdered in the past 30 years. Some politicians even sing “Kill the Boer” songs. Given the political and demographic realities, there are only so many Oranias one can build in South Africa and get away.

Lauren Southern’s documentary explores this South African farm attack phenomenon. It was chilling to watch.: Farmlands (2018).

P.S. Of all the things that have happened in the last few years, I find it interesting and weird that this story is what Tyler reacts to with such strong emotion.

item.title: Comment on “By your culture, we shall know ye” by SpeculativeDiction
item.description:
And look what specifically gets called out here: a drag show.

Has the left ever committed more disastrously to a losing cause than the Trans issue? It should be dropped from all left platforms immediately, it is toxic for holding onto the centre.

The approach to trans issues should be quiet tolerance, not noisy celebration. It is clear it is pure political kryptonite at this point.
